messages:
maria.infra: Heads-up — I sketched a proposal for a soft-degradation shaper for org/api keys that reacts to GPU saturation and queue length. Idea is to avoid hard 429s during short spikes and instead gradually degrade guarantees.
aj.sre: high-level summary? sounds useful if it's not too complex to operate.
maria.infra: tl;dr: each org gets a baseline token rate (steady-state). When node-level GPU saturation or long scheduler queue is observed, we compute a fleet stress factor S in [0,1]. We multiply per-org steady rate by (1 - alpha * S) where alpha is tunable per-tier. So traffic is throttled proportionally instead of all-or-nothing.
devon.platform: how do we compute S? single metric or composite?
maria.infra: composite — weighted sum: GPU_util_90p, pending_queue_depth_norm, avg_latency_p50_ratio. Pseudocode in short: ```S = clamp(w1*gpu90 + w2*queue_norm + w3*lat_ratio, 0,1)```
sam.ops: can we make it region-aware? some regions are saturated while others not.
maria.infra: yes — S computed per-region, and per-org shaping applied in the region where the requests arrive. If org has multi-region fallback, we allow soft-fallback routing.
kevin.ml: what about billing and fairness? big orgs could get penalized.
maria.infra: we keep two buckets: reserved (guaranteed) and elastic (subject to S). Reserved is minimal and depends on subscription tier. Elastic is what's scaled down when S>0. We also track reclaimed tokens to bill but mark as "degraded" in billing export so support can reconcile.
aj.sre: how do we handle long-running streaming requests that hold GPU? backpressure at admission time only?
maria.infra: yes — admission checks both estimated GPU-occupancy (based on model and requested max tokens) and current S. If admission passes but node drops below threshold mid-run we have graceful degradation: reduce chunk-rate, drop nonessential callbacks, and notify client via response header `X-Redwood-Degraded: true`.
devon.platform: curious about concrete refill algorithm. could we use token-bucket but with dynamic refill rate = base * (1 - alpha*S)?
maria.infra: exactly. Example config: ```org_shaper: { base_rps: 10, reserved_rps: 2, alpha: 0.8, warm_window_s: 30 }``` warm_window allows short bursts to pass before shaping clamps.
kevin.ml: sounds good. can we simulate on historical traffic?
maria.infra: yes I ran a 2-week replay on a 200k qps trace. Results: 15% reduction in 95p latency under identical load vs current hard-429 policy, with 2% extra tail 503 for non-reserved traffic. I'll post graphs to #eng-sre later.
sam.ops: rollout plan?
maria.infra: propose: 1) unit tests + sim harness; 2) dark-launch shaping control plane with metrics only for 2 days; 3) opt-in per-tenant beta; 4) gradual default on for lower tiers; 5) rollout to all with quick rollback.
aj.sre: obs — expose metrics: redwood.shaper.S, per-org_shaper.effective_rps, admission_drops{reason}, degraded_responses. Also add an alert when reclaimed_tokens_rate > threshold.
ops-bot: deploy-check: CI passed for shaper prototype. Integration tests: 12/15 ok, 3 flaky (queue edgecases) — tagging @maria.infra. :white_check_mark:
maria.infra: noted, I'll investigate the flaky tests. Quick question: do we want to return 429 or 503 when elastic tokens exhausted? My leaning: 429 for client-level throttles, 503 when fleet-level saturation so clients know it's systemic.
devon.platform: agree — 503 for fleet issues so clients can consider retry-after or fallback region. 429 for per-org quota exceed.
kevin.ml: can we include a Rate-Limit-Info header with fields: reserved, effective, degraded=true/false? helps clients adapt.
aj.sre: yes include headers: `X-RateLimit-Reserved`, `X-RateLimit-Effective`, `X-RateLimit-Degraded`. Keep them optional to reduce overhead.
sam.ops: cost note — if we route more to regions with spare capacity that increases egress costs. Need to add cost tag in routing decision.
maria.infra: added to TODO: routing_cost_weight in policy.
aj.sre: last — make sure audit log records when we throttle due to S and include sample of traces for debugging.
maria.infra: will add log line example: `INFO shaper: org=acme alpha=0.8 S=0.65 reserved=2 effective=0.7 reason=gpu90`
kevin.ml: this reads well. +1 to dark launch.
sam.ops: +1
devon.platform: can you open a PR with config proto and simulation results? I'll review.
maria.infra: PR incoming in ~1h. Thanks everyone :rocket:
